text: In my stars I am above thee, but be not afraid of greatness. Some are born great, some achieve greatness, and some have greatness thrust upon ’em.
location: Twelfth Night, Act 2 Scene 5
plain: Some are born great, some earn it, some get it dropped on them. Do not be afraid of greatness.

text: Foolery, sir, does walk about the orb like the sun; it shines everywhere.
location: Twelfth Night, Act 3 Scene 1
plain: Foolishness is everywhere, like the sun. Nobody is above it.

text:
A murd’rous guilt shows not itself more soon
Than love that would seem hid. Love’s night is noon.
location: Twelfth Night, Act 3 Scene 1
plain: Guilt shows itself fast, and so does love you are trying to hide.

text: Love sought is good, but given unsought is better.
location: Twelfth Night, Act 3 Scene 1
plain: Love you chase is good. Love that comes to you unasked is better.

text:
In nature there’s no blemish but the mind;
None can be call’d deform’d but the unkind.
Virtue is beauty, but the beauteous evil
Are empty trunks, o’erflourished by the devil.
location: Twelfth Night, Act 3 Scene 4
plain: The only real ugliness is a cold heart. Good looks can hide a rotten person.

text: I say there is no darkness but ignorance, in which thou art more puzzled than the Egyptians in their fog.
location: Twelfth Night, Act 4 Scene 2
plain: The only real darkness is not knowing.

text: Now my foes tell me plainly I am an ass: so that by my foes, sir, I profit in the knowledge of myself, and by my friends I am abused.
location: Twelfth Night, Act 5 Scene 1
plain: Enemies tell you the truth about yourself. Friends flatter you into being a fool.

text: And thus the whirligig of time brings in his revenges.
location: Twelfth Night, Act 5 Scene 1
plain: Time turns and everyone gets paid back eventually.

text:
Alas, it is the baseness of thy fear
That makes thee strangle thy propriety.
Fear not, Cesario, take thy fortunes up.
Be that thou know’st thou art, and then thou art
As great as that thou fear’st.
location: Twelfth Night, Act 5 Scene 1
plain: Fear is what keeps you small. Be who you know you are and you are as big as the thing you fear.

text: Home-keeping youth have ever homely wits.
location: The Two Gentlemen of Verona, Act 1 Scene 1
plain: Staying put makes you dull. You get sharp by going out.

text:
To be in love, where scorn is bought with groans,
Coy looks with heart-sore sighs, one fading moment’s mirth
With twenty watchful, weary, tedious nights.
If haply won, perhaps a hapless gain;
If lost, why then a grievous labour won;
However, but a folly bought with wit,
Or else a wit by folly vanquished.
location: The Two Gentlemen of Verona, Act 1 Scene 1
plain: Chasing love often costs more than it pays: it is a folly bought with wit, or wit beaten by folly.

location: The Two Gentlemen of Verona, Act 1 Scene 1
plain: If love is your master and you obey it, do not expect to be called wise.

text:
Thou, Julia, thou hast metamorphosed me,
Made me neglect my studies, lose my time,
War with good counsel, set the world at nought;
Made wit with musing weak, heart sick with thought.
location: The Two Gentlemen of Verona, Act 1 Scene 1
plain: Infatuation made me neglect my work, waste my time, and ignore good advice. My mind went weak.

text:
Fie, fie, how wayward is this foolish love
That like a testy babe will scratch the nurse
And presently, all humbled, kiss the rod!
location: The Two Gentlemen of Verona, Act 1 Scene 2
plain: Love makes you lash out at what you want, then crawl back and take the punishment.

text: Fire that’s closest kept burns most of all.
location: The Two Gentlemen of Verona, Act 1 Scene 2
plain: The fire you keep hidden burns hottest.

text:
I have no other but a woman’s reason:
I think him so because I think him so.
location: The Two Gentlemen of Verona, Act 1 Scene 2
plain: Sometimes the only reason is a feeling, and you cannot argue it.

text:
Experience is by industry achieved
And perfected by the swift course of time.
location: The Two Gentlemen of Verona, Act 1 Scene 3
plain: Experience comes from hard work and then time finishes it.

text:
Thus have I shunned the fire for fear of burning
And drenched me in the sea, where I am drowned.
location: The Two Gentlemen of Verona, Act 1 Scene 3
plain: Dodging the fire, I walked into the sea and drowned.

text:
O, how this spring of love resembleth
The uncertain glory of an April day,
Which now shows all the beauty of the sun,
And by an by a cloud takes all away.
location: The Two Gentlemen of Verona, Act 1 Scene 3
plain: Good things can be gone in a moment, like a cloud taking the sun on an April day.

text:
Except I be by Silvia in the night,
There is no music in the nightingale.
Unless I look on Silvia in the day,
There is no day for me to look upon.
location: The Two Gentlemen of Verona, Act 3 Scene 1
plain: Without the person you love, the whole world goes silent and dark.

text:
Cease to lament for that thou canst not help,
And study help for that which thou lament’st.
Time is the nurse and breeder of all good.
location: The Two Gentlemen of Verona, Act 3 Scene 1
plain: Stop mourning what you cannot help and work on what you can. Time heals most things.

text:
Hope is a lover’s staff; walk hence with that
And manage it against despairing thoughts.
location: The Two Gentlemen of Verona, Act 3 Scene 1
plain: Hope is the staff you walk with. Use it against despair.

text: How use doth breed a habit in a man!
location: The Two Gentlemen of Verona, Act 5 Scene 4
plain: Habit builds itself in you without asking.

text:
The private wound is deepest. O time most accurst,
’Mongst all foes that a friend should be the worst!
location: The Two Gentlemen of Verona, Act 5 Scene 4
plain: The deepest cuts come from a friend.

location: The Two Gentlemen of Verona, Act 5 Scene 4
plain: Real remorse deserves forgiveness. Refusing it puts you out of step with heaven and earth.

text:
O heaven, were man
But constant, he were perfect. That one error
Fills him with faults, makes him run through all th’ sins;
Inconstancy falls off ere it begins.
location: The Two Gentlemen of Verona, Act 5 Scene 4
plain: A person who stayed constant would be perfect. Wavering is the one flaw that breeds all the others.

text: But love will not be spurred to what it loathes.
location: The Two Gentlemen of Verona, Act 5 Scene 2
plain: Love cannot be forced.

text:
A thousand more mischances than this one
Have learned me how to brook this patiently.
location: The Two Gentlemen of Verona, Act 5 Scene 3
plain: A thousand worse breaks than this one taught me how to take it calmly.

text:
O grief and time,
Fearful consumers, you will all devour!
location: The Two Noble Kinsmen, Act 1 Scene 1
plain: Grief and time eat everything in the end.

text:
Extremity, that sharpens sundry wits,
Makes me a fool.
location: The Two Noble Kinsmen, Act 1 Scene 1
plain: Extreme pain sharpens some minds and turns others into fools. Do not judge people in it.

text:
Who cannot feel nor see the rain, being in ’t,
Knows neither wet nor dry.
location: The Two Noble Kinsmen, Act 1 Scene 1
plain: If you are standing in it, you cannot feel the rain. You are too deep to see it.

text:
As we are men,
Thus should we do; being sensually subdued,
We lose our human title.
location: The Two Noble Kinsmen, Act 1 Scene 1
plain: We are men only while we stay in control of ourselves. Lose control and you lose that.
